done_when: The worker brief lets a worker update any existing test its intended change breaks, outside its scope, naming each changed test and why in its handoff; the review brief no longer reports such test files as outside scope but reports a test weakened to hide a real defect as a P1; tests through forge work and forge close show both

findings.body: The new instruction asks the reviewer to check that the worker named and explained each changed test. But `forge close` passes a generated prompt and a fresh Git clone to review (`src/forge/review.py:285-298, 315-318`). Claude output goes to an uncommitted work log (`src/forge/worker.py:422-434`; `src/forge/repo.py:100-110`), while the Codex path records only a pending question from its final text (`src/forge/worker.py:178-181`). A handoff given only in the worker's final response is therefore unavailable to the reviewer. Pass the handoff into review or remove this unverifiable check.
findings.title: Reviewer cannot inspect the worker handoff it is told to verify

findings.body: This condition exempts every pre-existing test-shaped path without checking whether the intended work broke it. The new `forge close` test demonstrates the gap: it changes `app.py` to print a string and separately changes `tests/test_old.py` from `assert True` to `assert False`, then expects that test to be absent from the outside-Scope list (`tests/test_fix_workers_stop_to_ask_before_updating_an_e.py:58-60, 79-82`). Such an unrelated edit is outside the stated exception, so the review prompt should still identify it for scope review.
findings.title: Unrelated existing tests disappear from the outside-Scope list

why: Workers stop to ask before updating an existing test their intended change breaks, because the test file is outside the task's scope; it happened seven times on 2026-09-28
